findings.title: Periodic-tail surgery and an open seed-repair regeneration lemma
findings.claim: Proposed, unproved: for every actual-prefix periodic-tail surgery (T,P), its white-right-half inverse seed has a black cell in every sufficiently aligned dyadic annulus. Finite experiment tests M=2*(T+P+1).
findings.scope: Rule 30 from the single seed; initial right half white; u(t)=c(t) for t<T and c(T+((t-T) mod P)) thereafter. Finite grid T=0..16, P=1..16, trace and inverse-prefix lengths 2048. Infinite conjecture quantifies every T>=0,P>=1 and some M>=1, then all k>=0.
findings.result: All 1514 complete tested annuli in 272 cases contained an extra black seed cell. All finite controls passed. The stronger period-sized-window bound failed at T=0,P=1,m=1. No unbounded argument or new period exclusion was obtained.
limitations: Inverse realization and triangular sensitivity are existing kit results, not new findings; no Lean replay was performed here.
Finite observations do not imply infinite support, a density bound, the proposed regeneration lemma, or official Problem 1.
No proved boundary-state transition or OR/cancellation certificate is supplied; the conjecture may be false.
Periodic forcing cannot be assumed to stabilize or bound the driven right half.
The 272 pairs can prescribe duplicate traces and are not independent statistical evidence.
Rules 90, 150 and 210 controls require no extra seed edits, so generic left-permutivity is insufficient.
findings.next_action: Falsify the fixed-M rule on held-out onsets and periods, then seek a symbolic scale transition that retains the actual driven-right-column state and survives XOR cancellation; prove that transition before drawing an unbounded conclusion.
